```python
    llm=FunctionModel(always_call_tool),
    tools=[ping],
    middleware=[CountTurns(), ToolBudget(max_calls=2, message="Budget used.")],
)
result = agent.run("go")
assert result.stop_reason == "tool_budget"
```

## Memory (brief)

`Agent(memory=...)` takes any object with `get_context(query, max_messages)` and `add(message)`. Use `Memory(...)` (recommended; keyword-only: `location`, `user_id`, `agent_id`, `window`, `learn`, `summarize`, `recall`, `semantic`, `embedder`, `max_users`...) for a durable per-user store plus a conversation window; `AgentMemory(max_messages=)` is a plain sliding window; `ComposableMemory` mixes blocks. `Memory()` defaults to a local SQLite store. For many users, pass `user_id=lambda ctx: ...` and always call with `context=RunContext(...)`: a run whose resolver returns nothing gets no conversation memory (it is not shared with other users). `learn=llm` extracts durable facts from user messages only. The full surface (tiers, summaries, recall) is in the repo's `docs/agents/memory.md`; read it before using anything beyond the snippet.

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass

from fastaiagent import Agent, Memory, RunContext
from fastaiagent.testing import TestModel


@dataclass
class Session:
    user_id: str


llm = TestModel(response="noted")
agent = Agent(name="assistant", llm=llm, memory=Memory(user_id=lambda ctx: ctx.state.user_id))
ctx = RunContext(state=Session(user_id="ana"))
agent.run("My name is Ana", context=ctx)
agent.run("What is my name?", context=ctx)
assert "My name is Ana" in [m.content for m in llm.calls[1]["messages"]]
```

## Multimodal input (brief)

- `run`/`arun`/`astream` accept a string, an `Image`, a `PDF`, or a list mixing them: `agent.run(["What is in this?", Image.from_file("cat.jpg")])`. `stream()` accepts only `str`.
- Build parts with `Image.from_file(path)` / `from_url(url)` / `from_bytes(data, media_type)`, `PDF.from_file` / `from_url` / `from_bytes`, `File.from_url` / `from_bytes`. `Image.from_bytes` needs the media type as its second argument.
- The model must support the modality. `LLMClient(pdf_mode=, max_pdf_pages=, max_image_size_mb=)` tune PDF/image handling.

## Pitfalls

- `@tool` returns a `FunctionTool`, not the function: `get_weather("x")` raises `TypeError`. Call `.execute({...})` or keep a separate plain function.
- A tool that raises does not crash the run: the model receives `Error: Tool '<name>' failed: ...` and continues. Assert on `result.tool_calls`, not only on exceptions.
- `result.output` is only the last turn's text.

---

# Guardrails

Read this when you add input/output/tool checks to an agent, write a custom check, or need to know what blocks, what warns, and what a check that cannot run reports.

## The model

A guardrail is a check on a payload at one position. The SDK runs it locally, inside your process: a block always happens at the edge. A connected control plane can author and distribute rules, and the SDK enforces them next to your local `guardrails=[...]`; it never relies on the plane to stop a run.

```signature
fastaiagent.Guardrail(name, guardrail_type=, position=, config=, blocking=, description=, fn=, on_error=, origin=, action=, severity=, floor=)
fastaiagent.Guardrail.execute(data)
fastaiagent.Guardrail.aexecute(data)
```

- `position` (`GuardrailPosition`): `input` (before the model sees the user message), `output` (the reply), `tool_call` (before a tool runs; the payload is the JSON text `{"tool": name, "arguments": {...}}`), `tool_result` (the tool's output text). Strings work: `position="input"`; a misspelt value raises at construction.
- `guardrail_type` (`GuardrailType`): `code` (default; your `fn=`), `llm_judge`, `regex`, `schema`, `classifier`, `content_safety`, `groundedness`, `topic`, `pii`, `secrets`. Import both enums from `fastaiagent.guardrail`.
- `blocking=True` (default): runs inline, in order, and a failing check halts. `blocking=False`: observe-only, runs in parallel, never halts and never rewrites.
- Attach with `Agent(..., guardrails=[...])`. A `Supervisor` takes its own `guardrails=` too (see `teams.md`).
- `fn(text)` returns a `bool` or a `GuardrailResult(passed, score=, message=, metadata=)`. A dict payload is passed to `fn` as JSON text.
- `execute` is sync. Inside async code use `await guardrail.aexecute(...)`.
- A blocking failure raises `GuardrailBlockedError` out of `agent.run()`. Import it with `from fastaiagent import GuardrailBlockedError` (it has `.guardrail_name`, `.results` and `.trace_id`, the blocked run's trace, `None` when tracing is off). Code written for 1.103.0 or earlier imports it from `fastaiagent._internal.errors`, which still works.

## Built-in factories

All live in `fastaiagent.guardrail`; each returns a `Guardrail` (`responsible_ai` returns a list).

```signature
fastaiagent.guardrail.no_pii(position=, entities=, backend=)
fastaiagent.guardrail.no_secrets(position=)
fastaiagent.guardrail.no_prompt_injection(position=, mode=, llm=, on_error=)
fastaiagent.guardrail.json_valid(position=)
fastaiagent.guardrail.toxicity_check(position=, mode=, llm=, threshold=, on_error=)
fastaiagent.guardrail.openai_moderation(position=, client=, model=, on_error=)
fastaiagent.guardrail.banned_topics(topics, llm=, mode=, position=, on_error=)
fastaiagent.guardrail.allowed_topics(topics, llm=, mode=, position=, on_error=)
fastaiagent.guardrail.grounded(reference, llm=, threshold=, position=, on_error=)
fastaiagent.guardrail.no_hallucination(reference, llm=, threshold=, position=, on_error=)
fastaiagent.guardrail.cost_limit(max_usd, position=, on_error=)
fastaiagent.guardrail.allowed_domains(domains, position=)
fastaiagent.guardrail.responsible_ai(pii=, prompt_injection=, secrets=, toxicity=, moderation=, grounded_to=, banned=, allowed=, llm=, threshold=, on_error=)
```

| Factory | Default position | Needs a model/key? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_pii` | output | no | `entities` default `("email","phone","ssn","credit_card")`; credit cards Luhn-checked; `"ip"`, `"iban"` opt-in; `backend="presidio"` needs `pip install "fastaiagent[safety]"` |
| `no_secrets` | output | no | private keys, AWS/GitHub/Slack/Google/OpenAI/Stripe tokens, JWTs, `api_key = "..."`; matches are masked in metadata |
| `no_prompt_injection` | input | heuristic: no; `mode="llm"`/`"decisions"`: yes | `on_error` default `"allow"` |
| `json_valid` | output | no | output must parse as JSON |
| `toxicity_check` | output | keyword: no; `mode="llm"`/`"decisions"`: yes | blocks when score >= `threshold` (0.5); `on_error` default `"allow"` |
| `openai_moderation` | output | yes: `OPENAI_API_KEY` + `openai` package | `on_error` default `"block"` |
| `banned_topics` | output | `mode="keyword"`: no; `mode="llm"` (default): yes | `topics` = names, `{name, description}` pairs, or a name->description dict; `on_error` default `"allow"` |
| `allowed_topics` | output | `mode="keyword"`: no; `mode="llm"` (default): yes | whitelist; `on_error` default `"block"` (a whitelist that cannot classify must not pass) |
| `grounded` / `no_hallucination` (same function) | output | yes | `reference` is a string or a zero-arg callable evaluated at check time; no reference -> passes with "groundedness skipped"; `on_error` default `"block"`; threshold 0.7 |
| `cost_limit` | output | no | blocks when run spend > `max_usd`; an unpriced model RAISES (so `on_error` decides, default `"block"`) |
| `allowed_domains` | tool_call | no | host must equal or be a subdomain of an entry; `evilexample.com` does not match `example.com` |
| `responsible_ai` | mixed | default bundle: no | list: injection (input) + PII + secrets (output) on by default; LLM-backed rails are opt-in; spread it: `guardrails=responsible_ai(...)` |

`banned_topics` / `allowed_topics` in `mode="llm"` with no live-client `llm=` produce a `topic`-type rule; with `mode="keyword"` or a live `LLMClient` they stay a local `code` rule.

`mode="keyword"` is a word match: it needs no model, and it passes any text that contains a listed word ("tell me a joke about my order" passes an order-topics whitelist). Use it for offline tests or a coarse first line, and tell the user so; use `mode="llm"` when the meaning matters. A blocked run raises `GuardrailBlockedError` to the caller; an application should catch it and answer the person, not crash.

```python
from fastaiagent import Agent, GuardrailBlockedError
from fastaiagent.guardrail import banned_topics, json_valid, no_pii, no_secrets
from fastaiagent.testing import TestModel

assert no_pii().execute("call me on 123-45-6789").passed is False
assert json_valid().execute('{"a": 1}').passed is True
assert banned_topics(["politics"], mode="keyword").execute("let's discuss politics").passed is False
assert no_secrets().execute('api_key = "sk-proj-abcdefghijklmnopqrst"').passed is False

agent = Agent(name="bot", llm=TestModel(response="SSN is 123-45-6789"), guardrails=[no_pii()])
try:
    agent.run("hi")
except GuardrailBlockedError as err:
    assert err.guardrail_name == "no_pii"
```

A tool-call gate runs before the tool executes (the tool never runs on a block):

```python
from fastaiagent import Agent, FunctionTool, GuardrailBlockedError
from fastaiagent.guardrail import allowed_domains
from fastaiagent.testing import FunctionModel

fetched = []
def fetch(url: str) -> str:
    fetched.append(url)
    return "page"

calls = {"n": 0}
def model(messages):
    calls["n"] += 1
    if calls["n"] == 1:
        return "", [{"name": "fetch", "arguments": {"url": "https://evil.com/x"}}]
    return "done"

agent = Agent(name="web", llm=FunctionModel(model),
              tools=[FunctionTool(name="fetch", fn=fetch, description="Fetch a URL")],
              guardrails=[allowed_domains(["api.mycompany.com"])])
try:
    agent.run("go")
except GuardrailBlockedError:
    assert fetched == []
```

## Config-driven types (survive serialization and distribution)

`Guardrail(guardrail_type=..., config={...})`. These round-trip through `to_dict()`/`from_dict()` and are what a control plane distributes. A `code` rule's `fn=` cannot be serialized.

| Type | Key `config` fields |
|---|---|
| `regex` | `pattern`, `should_match` (default False: a match fails), `case_insensitive`, `mask_token`, `timeout_seconds` (ReDoS bound; a timeout FAILS, it does not allow) |
| `schema` | `schema` (or `json_schema`): a non-empty JSON Schema dict; validated with `jsonschema` (a core dependency) |
| `classifier` | `categories` {name: [keywords]}, optional `blocked` list (absent = every detected category blocks) |
| `pii` | `entities` list, `backend` (`regex` or `presidio`) |
| `secrets` | none, by design |
| `topic` | `topics`, `mode` (`deny` default, or `allow`), `backend` |
| `content_safety` | `categories` (S1..S14), `threshold`, `thresholds` per category, `backend` |
| `groundedness` | `context_key`, `answer_key`, `threshold` (0.7) |
| `llm_judge` | `prompt` (or `backend: "decisions"` + `instructions` + `threshold`), `pass_value` (`PASS`), `llm` |

`config["llm"]` takes shareable `LLMClient` kwargs only; an `api_key` there raises at construction. Model-backed judges need a key in the environment (`# needs: OPENAI_API_KEY` or the provider you configured).

## on_error, action, severity

Three independent axes: `blocking` (does it run inline and halt?), `on_error` (what does a check that COULD NOT RUN mean?), `action` (what does a genuine failure cost?).

- `on_error="block"` (default on `Guardrail`): a check that errors fails closed. `"allow"`: fails open. An errored result has `errored=True` either way, so a degraded pass is distinguishable: `passed=True, errored=True` is NOT a genuine pass. Check `result.errored`, not just `result.passed`.
- `action` is one of `block` (default), `warn`, `mask`, `override`, `reask`. An unknown value becomes `block`.
  - `warn`: record and continue. `mask`: replace the offending spans with `config["mask_token"]` (default `[REDACTED]`) and continue; only `regex`, `classifier`, `pii`, `secrets` can mask, and a mask with nothing to redact BLOCKS. `override`: replace the payload with `config["override_message"]` and continue. `reask`: re-prompt the model with the failure, up to `AgentConfig.guardrail_retries` (default 1); exhausting it blocks; at any position other than output, or when streaming, it blocks.
  - An errored check always blocks regardless of `action`. A rewrite the run cannot apply (a streamed reply, multimodal input) blocks instead of passing the payload through.
- Branch on `result.action_taken` (`none|blocked|warned|masked|overridden|reask`), never on the configured `result.action`. `result.modified_data` holds the rewrite.
- `severity` (`low|medium|high|critical`) and `floor` are carried and traced; nothing in local enforcement depends on them (`floor` is plane governance).
- Every run's guardrail firings are on `AgentResult.guardrails` (a `GuardrailFiring` has `name`, `position`, `action_taken`, `effect`, `passed`, `errored`). Use `firing.fired()` to find rules that did anything. `warn`/`mask` are only visible there.

```python
from fastaiagent import Agent, Guardrail
from fastaiagent.guardrail import GuardrailPosition, GuardrailType
from fastaiagent.testing import TestModel

redact = Guardrail(
    name="redact-ssn",
    guardrail_type=GuardrailType.regex,
    position=GuardrailPosition.output,
    config={"pattern": r"\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b", "mask_token": "[SSN]"},
    action="mask",
)
agent = Agent(name="bot", llm=TestModel(response="SSN is 123-45-6789"), guardrails=[redact])
result = agent.run("hi")
assert result.output == "SSN is [SSN]"
assert [(g.name, g.action_taken) for g in result.guardrails] == [("redact-ssn", "masked")]
```

## A check that cannot check must say so

> A guardrail whose configuration cannot check anything reports that it could not run (`errored=True`, decided by `on_error`) — never a clean pass.

Do NOT write a rule that returns `passed=True` when it has nothing to inspect — because a green rule over an unchecked payload reads as a healthy control. The runners already enforce this for config-driven types: an empty schema, `pii` with `entities: []` or an unknown entity, `regex` with no/empty/uncompilable pattern, `classifier` with no categories, `topic` with no topics or a mistyped `mode`, `content_safety` with only unknown categories, `groundedness` with no context, and `code` with no `fn` (for example after `from_dict`) all report `errored=True` and block under the default `on_error`.

```python
from fastaiagent import Guardrail
from fastaiagent.guardrail import GuardrailType

rule = Guardrail(name="empty-pii", guardrail_type=GuardrailType.pii,
                 config={"entities": []}, on_error="block")
result = rule.execute("my ssn is 123-45-6789")
assert result.errored and not result.passed

fail_open = Guardrail(name="empty-pii", guardrail_type=GuardrailType.pii,
                      config={"entities": []}, on_error="allow")
result = fail_open.execute("my ssn is 123-45-6789")
assert result.errored and result.passed  # a degraded pass, not a verdict
```

- When you add a new distributable type or a new config switch, add an unusable-config case to `tests/test_guardrail_unusable_config_sweep.py`; that sweep fails if a distributable type has none (`secrets` and `llm_judge` are exempt).
- Parameterised builtins (`cost_limit`, `allowed_domains`, `grounded`) and your own `fn=` do NOT survive `from_dict`: they come back with no callable and raise at execution rather than pass. Zero-argument builtins (`no_pii`, `no_secrets`, `json_valid`, `toxicity_check`, `no_prompt_injection`, `openai_moderation`) come back armed.

## guardrail_context

An output guardrail sees only the answer. A `groundedness` rule scores that answer against the context it should have used, taken from a run-scoped slot (per task, via `ContextVar`):

```python
# needs: OPENAI_API_KEY
import fastaiagent as fa
from fastaiagent import Agent, Guardrail, LLMClient
from fastaiagent.guardrail import GuardrailPosition, GuardrailType

rule = Guardrail(
    name="grounded-answer",
    guardrail_type=GuardrailType.groundedness,
    position=GuardrailPosition.output,
    config={"context_key": "context", "threshold": 0.7},
)
agent = Agent(name="qa", llm=LLMClient(provider="openai", model="gpt-4o-mini"), guardrails=[rule])
with fa.guardrail_context(context=["Refunds take 5 business days."]):
    reply = agent.run("How long do refunds take?")
```

```signature
fastaiagent.guardrail_context(**values)
fastaiagent.set_guardrail_context(**values)
fastaiagent.get_guardrail_context()
fastaiagent.clear_guardrail_context(token)
```

Do wrap the run in `with fa.guardrail_context(...)`. Don't rely on it being set: a `groundedness` rule that finds no context raises (could-not-run), it does not pass. For a locally written rule `grounded(lambda: latest_docs)` is the callable equivalent.

## Local versus control plane

- The SDK executes: every type above runs in-process. A connected agent also turns plane-authored rules (`regex`, `schema`, `classifier`, `llm_judge`, `content_safety`, `groundedness`, `topic`, `pii`, `secrets`) into `Guardrail(origin="plane")` at all four positions; a plane `code` rule is skipped because its logic is not distributable.
- Plane-authored rules are enforced alongside local ones. `floor` and draft/publish governance are plane concepts; locally `floor` is only displayed.

### Plane-authored rules on a connected agent

You do not fetch them or pass them in. `connect()` pulls the policy once, and every run adds the
rules that apply to that agent to its own `guardrails=[...]`. What you write is the check that they
arrived:

```python
# needs: a connected plane with at least one active guardrail rule
import os

import fastaiagent as fa
from fastaiagent import Agent, GuardrailBlockedError, LLMClient

fa.connect(api_key=os.environ["FASTAIAGENT_API_KEY"], target=os.environ["FASTAIAGENT_TARGET"])
try:
    agent = Agent(name="support", llm=LLMClient(provider="openai", model="gpt-5-mini"))
    agent.push()  # registers it now, so its id is known before you list its rules
    plane_rules = fa.plane_guardrails_for_agent(agent.agent_id)
    print([(g.name, g.position.value) for g in plane_rules])
    try:
        agent.run("an input one of those rules should block")
    except GuardrailBlockedError as err:
        print("blocked by", err.guardrail_name, "trace", err.trace_id)  # read this trace back
finally:
    fa.disconnect()
```

- **When they change.** The policy is not re-pulled by itself. A rule authored or edited after
  `connect()` applies after `fa.refresh_policy()`; the next run rebuilds the list.
- **Which ones apply.** A rule with no agents attached is domain-wide. A rule attached to agents
  applies to those plane agent ids only. `plane_guardrails_for_agent` takes the id, or the name of
  an agent this process has pushed. An agent gets its id when it registers, which a connected
  agent does on its first run; that run waits for it (up to 5 s) when rules are attached to agents.
  If registration takes longer, a warning says the attached rules were not applied to that run.
  The plane identifies an agent by name, so a new agent that reuses an existing name in the
  domain gets that agent's rules: pick a name that is not taken.
- **An empty list is not a pass.** It means none apply, the rule was authored after `connect()`,
  it is a `code` rule (skipped), or the policy pull failed. A failed pull is logged as a warning
  and keeps the last policy, so read the log and say what you saw; do not say the rules are
  enforced.
- **Do not copy them into code.** Do not rebuild a plane rule locally or pass the result of
  `plane_guardrails_for_agent` into `guardrails=[...]`. Plane rules are never pushed back with the
  agent's definition.
- **Testing.** An offline test with `TestModel` sees no plane rules, and a test that passes a local
  guardrail (`no_pii()`, a regex) in their place tests that guardrail, not the plane's. Put the
  test that proves a plane rule fires in `tests/e2e/`, marked `e2e`, skipped when
  `FASTAIAGENT_TARGET` is not set, and do not add a `guardrails=` parameter only to fake it.
- **Evidence.** Each check is a guardrail span on the run's trace, which reaches the plane with the
  trace. The plane's own guardrail views are read in the console, not through the SDK.
- SDK-only: `action="reask"`, `guardrail_context`, `timeout_seconds` and the regex ReDoS bound, and `code` rules via `fn=`.
- Traces: local capture is full fidelity. Guardrail span detail leaving the process is an allowlist per type; setting `FASTAIAGENT_TRACE_PAYLOADS=0` stops payload-bearing attributes from being exported.
- Test offline with `TestModel` / `FunctionModel` (see `teams.md`); keep tests of model-backed judges in `tests/e2e/` marked `e2e`.

---

# Evals, scorers, pytest gates and the eval CLI

Read this when you score an agent against a dataset, write a scorer or an LLM judge, add `@case` / `evaluate_one` tests, gate CI on quality, or run `fastaiagent eval`.

## evaluate()

```text
from fastaiagent.eval import evaluate
evaluate(agent_fn, dataset, scorers=None, concurrency=4, persist=True, run_name=None, dataset_name=None, agent_name=None, run_kind="evaluate", **kwargs)
```

```signature
fastaiagent.eval.Dataset.from_jsonl(path)
fastaiagent.eval.Dataset.from_csv(path)
fastaiagent.eval.Dataset.from_list(items)
fastaiagent.eval.Dataset.to_jsonl(path, append=)
```

- `agent_fn` is any callable taking the input and returning a string or an `AgentResult` (`agent.run` is the usual value). Sync callables run on a worker thread; async callables are awaited. `dataset` is a `Dataset`, a list of dicts, or a `.jsonl` / `.csv` path (anything else is read as JSONL).
- Row keys: `input` (required), `expected_output` or `expected`, and the per-row scorer inputs `expected_trajectory`, `expected_tool_calls`, `expected_steps`, `context`, `contexts`. Other keys are ignored. Extra `**kwargs` to `evaluate()` go to every scorer for every row; a row's own value wins.
- `scorers` defaults to `["exact_match"]`. Names are strings or `Scorer` instances. An unknown name, a name needing constructor arguments (`regex_match`), or two scorers with the same `name` raises `EvalError` before any agent call.
- `persist=True` (default) writes the run to `./.fastaiagent/local.db`. Pass `persist=False` in tests and one-off scripts. The async twin is `from fastaiagent.eval.evaluate import aevaluate`.
- An agent that raises or pauses (approval, `interrupt()`) makes the case **errored**: it is not scored and not counted as a quality failure. A scorer that raises is recorded as errored for that case; it does not abort the run.

Every scorer verdict has an `outcome`: `passed`, `failed`, `errored` (could not run: judge outage, unparseable reply, scorer bug) or `skipped` (does not apply: no expected output, no trajectory). Rates exclude errored and skipped. Never read an errored check as a failure or as a pass.

```python
from fastaiagent import Agent
from fastaiagent.eval import evaluate, gate
from fastaiagent.testing import FunctionModel

agent = Agent(name="capitals", llm=FunctionModel(
    lambda msgs: "Paris" if "France" in str(msgs[-1].content) else "Rome"))

cases = [
    {"input": "Capital of France?", "expected_output": "Paris"},
    {"input": "Capital of Italy?", "expected": "Rome"},
    {"input": "Capital of Spain?", "expected_output": "Madrid"},
]
results = evaluate(agent.run, cases, scorers=["exact_match", "contains"], persist=False)
print(results.summary())
report = gate(results, fail_under=["exact_match=0.5"], max_error_rate=0.1)
assert report.outcome == "passed", report.describe()
assert gate(results, fail_under=["exact_match=0.9"]).outcome == "failed"
```

## Built-in scorers

String names usable in `scorers=[...]` and `--scorers`:

- Offline, no key: `exact_match`, `contains` (case-insensitive substring), `json_valid`, `length_between`, `latency`, `cost_under`, `pii_leakage`, `prompt_injection`, `bleu`, `rouge`, `levenshtein`.
- Need an LLM (default `LLMClient()` unless you build the instance with `llm=`): `faithfulness`, `answer_relevancy`, `context_precision`, `context_recall`, `toxicity`, `bias`, `task_completion`, `hallucination`, `reflection_quality`. `moderation` calls the OpenAI moderation API.
- `semantic_similarity` embeds with fastembed if installed, else OpenAI, else a crude `SimpleEmbedder` (silent fallback; scores then mean little).
- Needs an argument, so instance only: `RegexMatch(pattern)`. Pass instances to set non-default options on the others, e.g. `LengthBetween(min_len=, max_len=)`, `Latency(max_ms=)`, `CostUnder(max_usd=)`, `Faithfulness(llm=, threshold=)`.
- Instances only, not resolvable by name: `LLMJudge`, `GEval`, `DecisionJudge`, trajectory scorers (`ToolUsageAccuracy`, `StepEfficiency`, `PathCorrectness`, `CycleEfficiency`, `ToolCallCorrectness`) and session scorers (`ConversationCoherence`, `GoalCompletion`, `KnowledgeRetention`, `RoleAdherence`, `ConversationRelevancy`). All import from `fastaiagent.eval`.
- Trajectory scorers read the agent's real tool calls from the `AgentResult` plus the row's `expected_trajectory`; with no expected value they are `skipped`, and with a plain-string agent output they are `errored`. `evaluate()` does not forward a row's `conversation`: pass it as an `evaluate(..., conversation=...)` keyword or call the session scorer's `.score(...)` yourself.
- `latency` and `cost_under` use run facts `evaluate()` supplies. `cost_under` is **errored** (not passed) when the model has no known price, because unknown cost is not free cost.

## Custom scorers

```signature
fastaiagent.eval.Scorer.code(name=)
fastaiagent.eval.ScorerResult.error(reason, **details)
fastaiagent.eval.ScorerResult.not_applicable(reason, **details)
```

`@Scorer.code("name")` turns a plain function into a scorer. The function gets keyword arguments `input`, `output`, `expected` (optional) and may declare any of the extra kwargs it wants (`latency_ms`, `cost`, `actual_trajectory`, `context`, ...); undeclared extras are dropped unless it takes `**kwargs`. Return a `bool` (passed), a `float` (score; passed when `>= 0.5`), a `ScorerResult`, or anything else (recorded as a failed verdict with `str(result)` as the reason). Use `ScorerResult.not_applicable(...)` when the row lacks what you need and `ScorerResult.error(...)` when the check could not run. Don't return a clean pass for a check that could not run.

```python
from fastaiagent.eval import Scorer, ScorerResult, evaluate

@Scorer.code("is_short")
def is_short(input, output, expected=None):
    return len(output) < 20

@Scorer.code("mentions_expected")
def mentions_expected(input, output, expected=None, **kwargs):
    if expected is None:
        return ScorerResult.not_applicable("row has no expected output")
    ok = expected.lower() in output.lower()
    return ScorerResult(score=1.0 if ok else 0.0, passed=ok, reason=f"wanted {expected!r}")

results = evaluate(
    lambda text: "Paris",
    [{"input": "Capital of France?", "expected": "Paris"}],
    scorers=[is_short, mentions_expected],
    persist=False,
)
assert results.cases[0].per_scorer["mentions_expected"]["passed"] is True
```

Subclass `Scorer` (set `name`, implement `score(self, input, output, expected=None, **kwargs) -> ScorerResult`) when the scorer needs state or constructor arguments.

## LLM judge

```signature
fastaiagent.eval.LLMJudge(criteria=, prompt_template=, llm=, scale=, evaluation_steps=, rubric=, threshold=, name=, auto_steps=)
fastaiagent.eval.GEval(name=, criteria=, evaluation_steps=, rubric=, scale=, threshold=, llm=, auto_steps=)
```

`LLMJudge(criteria="correctness", llm=...)` makes one call, normalises the verdict from `scale` (`"binary"` default, `"0-1"`, `"1-5"`, `"1-10"`) to 0-1, and passes when `score >= threshold` (default 0.5). Passing `evaluation_steps` or `rubric` (list of `(score, description)`) switches to G-Eval mode; `GEval` is that mode by default on a `1-5` scale. A custom `prompt_template` must contain `{input}`, `{output}` or `{expected}`, else the judge never sees the content (a `UserWarning`). Always pass `llm=` explicitly; with `llm=None` it builds a default `LLMClient()` that needs a provider key. An unparseable reply is retried once, then recorded as errored; a judge outage is errored too, so a gate on it is `invalid`, not `failed`. In offline tests use a `TestModel` that returns the JSON verdict:

```python
from fastaiagent.eval import LLMJudge
from fastaiagent.testing import TestModel

judge = LLMJudge(
    criteria="helpfulness",
    llm=TestModel(response='{"score": 1, "reasoning": "answers the question"}'),
)
verdict = judge.score(input="2+2?", output="4", expected="4")
assert verdict.passed and verdict.outcome == "passed"

bad = LLMJudge(llm=TestModel(response="no json here")).score(input="q", output="a")
assert bad.outcome == "errored" and not bad.passed
```

## Gates

```text
from fastaiagent.eval import gate
gate(results, *, fail_under=None, max_error_rate=None) -> GateReport
```

`gate()` returns a `GateReport` with `.outcome` (`"passed"`, `"failed"`, `"invalid"`), `.describe()` (reason lines), `.checks`, `.scored`, `.errored`, `.error_rate`. Threshold strings, all `metric=value`:

- `overall.pass_rate=0.9`: share of applicable checks passed across all scorers.
- `cases.pass_rate=0.8`: share of cases where every applicable check passed.
- `<scorer>.avg_score=0.7` or `<scorer>.pass_rate=0.9`; a bare `<scorer>=0.9` means its pass rate.
- `overall.avg_score` is not a metric: it raises `EvalError`.

A run is `invalid` (not `failed`) when `max_error_rate` is exceeded, nothing was scored, a gated scorer errored on some cases and `max_error_rate` is unset or exceeded, or a gated named scorer applied to no case. `invalid` outranks `failed`. A threshold naming a scorer the run did not produce **fails**, so a typo never greens a build. Do set `max_error_rate` whenever any scorer is an LLM judge or the dataset can trigger approvals. Don't gate on one run when the agent is stochastic and the dataset is small: a single run can pass or fail on the model's luck.

**What an offline eval proves.** With `TestModel` or `FunctionModel` the agent's answers are
scripted, so a gate over them proves the wiring (the dataset loads, the scorer runs, the gate
fails when it should) and never the quality of the agent. A scripted model that echoes the tool's
output scores 100% by construction. Say that in your summary, and keep the quality eval as a
separate `e2e`-marked run against a real model (skipped without a key, and reported as skipped).

## pytest plugin

Installing `fastaiagent` plus `pytest` registers the plugin automatically (entry point `pytest11`); tests that do not use it are unaffected. `pytest` itself is not a fastaiagent dependency. Not xdist-aware: run eval-gated suites in one process.

```python
from fastaiagent import Agent
from fastaiagent.eval import case, pytest_dataset
from fastaiagent.testing import FunctionModel

agent = Agent(name="capitals", llm=FunctionModel(
    lambda msgs: "Paris" if "France" in str(msgs[-1].content) else "Rome"))

@case(input="Capital of France?", expected="Paris")
def test_france(evaluate_one):
    evaluate_one(agent.run, scorers=["exact_match", "contains"])

@pytest_dataset("cases.jsonl")          # one pytest test per row; file read at import time
def test_rows(eval_case, evaluate_one):  # eval_case is the row dict
    evaluate_one(agent.run, scorers=["exact_match"])
```

```signature
fastaiagent.eval.case(input, expected=, name=)
fastaiagent.eval.pytest_dataset(path, ids_from=)
```

`evaluate_one(agent_fn, *, input=None, expected=None, scorers=None, assert_pass=True, case_name=None, persist=True)` is a fixture returning a callable. Input and expected resolve from explicit args, then `@case`, then the dataset row. It returns the `EvalCaseRecord` (`.actual_output`, `.per_scorer`, `.trace_id`). Rules:

- Pass a **sync** callable (`agent.run`). `agent.arun` is not awaited: its coroutine is stringified and the case just fails.
- The test fails on a failed case, and also on an errored case (scorer could not run, none applied, agent raised or paused); the message says which. Pass `assert_pass=False` to inspect the record yourself.
- `scorers=None` means `exact_match`. A case with no expected value then has no applicable check and is errored; pass `contains`, `json_valid` or an instance that does not need `expected`.
- `case_name` and `@case(name=)` are accepted but have no effect (verified in source). `persist=False` keeps the case out of the stored run but it still counts for the gates.
- Row keys `expected_trajectory`, `context`, ... and the agent's tool calls reach scorers as in `evaluate()`.

All `evaluate_one` cases in a session aggregate into ONE stored run named `pytest::<rootdir name>`. Options (no option means no gating, but the run is still stored):

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--eval-fail-under METRIC=VALUE` | Threshold (grammar above). Repeatable. Malformed value is a usage error before any test runs. |
| `--eval-max-error-rate RATE` | Max fraction of errored cases before the session verdict is `invalid`. |
| `--eval-baseline RUN` | `run_id` or `run_name` of a stored run to compare with. |
| `--eval-tolerance DELTA` | Allowed overall pass-rate drop vs the baseline (default `0.0`). |
| `--eval-run-name NAME` | Name this session's stored run (default `pytest::<rootdir name>`). |

A breached gate raises a passing session's exit status to 1 and prints `GATE: ...` lines and a last line `fastaiagent eval verdict: PASSED|FAILED|INVALID`. It never lowers a failing status. A name baseline skips stored runs whose verdict was `failed` or `invalid`, so a regression cannot become the next baseline. `--eval-run-name main --eval-baseline main` is a ratchet: the baseline is resolved before this session is stored, and the first run (no accepted `main` yet) publishes it, gated on thresholds only. A baseline that cannot be loaded makes the session `invalid`.

Publish on the default branch, gate pull requests against it, and keep ONE database across both steps:

```bash
export FASTAIAGENT_LOCAL_DB=.ci/local.db      # same path in both jobs (cache it between runs)
pytest tests/evals --eval-run-name main
pytest tests/evals --eval-fail-under "overall.pass_rate=0.9" --eval-max-error-rate 0.1 \
       --eval-baseline main --eval-tolerance 0.02
```

Don't isolate the DB per test with a monkeypatch fixture for these suites: the session run is stored after the patch is undone, so it lands in the default DB and baselines are never found.

## CLI

```bash
fastaiagent eval run --agent app/agents.py:support --dataset cases.jsonl \
  --scorers exact_match,contains --fail-under "overall.pass_rate=0.9" \
  --max-error-rate 0.1 --run-name pr --json report.json
fastaiagent eval compare main pr --tolerance 0.02
```

`eval run` options: `--dataset` and `--agent` (both required; `path/file.py:attr` or `pkg.module:attr`, an `Agent` or a callable), `--scorers` (comma-separated built-in names, default `exact_match`; no instances, so no `regex_match`, no `LLMJudge`), `--concurrency` (4), `--run-name`, `--fail-under` (repeatable), `--max-error-rate`, `--json PATH` (report with `scorecard` and `gate`), `--no-persist`, `--db`. `eval compare BASELINE CURRENT` takes run ids or names (latest wins); `--tolerance`, `--fail-on-regression/--no-fail-on-regression`, `--db`. Also `eval curate` (turn captured traces into a dataset) and `eval export --dry-run` (print what a connected run would send).

| `eval run` exit | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Gate passed (also when no `--fail-under` and something was scored) |
| `1` | Quality gate failed (including a misspelled scorer in `--fail-under`) |
| `2` | Usage error from the CLI: missing option, malformed `--agent` spec, or the module has no such attribute |
| `3` | Run invalid: error rate over `--max-error-rate`, nothing scored, gated scorer could not run, unknown or argument-needing scorer name, `overall.avg_score`, dataset file missing, agent module fails to import |

`eval compare` exits `1` on a pass-rate drop beyond `--tolerance` and `3` when a run is not found.

## With a platform

Evals always run in your process, with your model keys. A connected plane can supply datasets and
judge configurations and receives the verdicts.

| What | How |
|---|---|
| Pull a dataset | `Dataset.from_platform(name)`, then pass it to `evaluate` |
| Push a dataset | `Dataset([...]).publish(name)` |
| Pull a judge | `Scorer.from_platform(name)` returns an `LLMJudge` (criteria, prompt template, scale); it runs locally. An unknown name raises `PlatformNotFoundError`. |
| Send a verdict | A **gated** run only (below) |
| Run an eval the plane asks for | `fastaiagent runner` executes the plane's `eval_run` jobs in your process (`platform.md`); for an agent built in Agent Studio, `fastaiagent studio eval` (the `fastaiagent-studio` skill) |

**A run is sent only once its gate verdict is recorded.** `evaluate()` followed by `gate()` sends
nothing: the run waits in `local.db`. The `fastaiagent eval run` CLI and the pytest plugin record
the verdict for you. In Python, record it yourself:

```python
# needs: a connected plane; the API key needs the eval:execute scope
import os

import fastaiagent as fa
from fastaiagent import Agent, Dataset, LLMClient
from fastaiagent.eval import evaluate, gate, record_gate_result

fa.connect(api_key=os.environ["FASTAIAGENT_API_KEY"], target=os.environ["FASTAIAGENT_TARGET"])
try:
    agent = Agent(name="support", llm=LLMClient(provider="openai", model="gpt-5-mini"))
    results = evaluate(agent.run, Dataset.from_platform("support-regression"), scorers=["contains"])
    report = gate(results, fail_under=["contains.pass_rate=0.9"], max_error_rate=0.1)
    record_gate_result(
        results.run_id, gate_outcome=report.outcome, thresholds={"contains.pass_rate": 0.9}
    )
    print(report.outcome, results.run_id)
finally:
    fa.disconnect()  # also sends the queued verdict
```

- **Only real runs are sent.** The plane counts a recorded verdict as evidence about the agent, and
  a run that `TestModel` or `FunctionModel` answered or judged scores what you scripted. The SDK
  keeps such a run local: `evaluate()` and the pytest plugin mark it (`scripted_models` in the run's
  local metadata), it is never queued, and `record_gate_result()` logs a warning when connected. Do
  not work around that. With no model key, stop and say the eval could not run; a scripted run
  is not a substitute.
- Only metadata leaves: aggregates, the verdict, thresholds, git provenance and per-case scorer
  verdicts with their `trace_id`. Inputs and outputs never do; the plane joins them from traces.
- The key needs the `eval:execute` scope, which is not a default. Without it (or without the
  domain's `connected_state_plane` entitlement) the plane answers 403, the SDK warns once and the
  run stays queued. `connect(export_evals=False)` or `FASTAIAGENT_EXPORT_EVALS=0` keeps every run
  local, and the plane cannot override that.
- The CLI and pytest plugin do not call `connect()`. Their verdicts are sent only when something in
  the same process connected (for example the agent module or `conftest.py`). Otherwise they wait
  in `local.db` and go with the next connected gated run.
- Check before claiming: after `disconnect()`, `fastaiagent eval export --status` shows how many runs
  are still waiting. A run leaves that count only when the plane has confirmed it, so 0 means it
  arrived. `--dry-run` prints the exact payload and names runs that have no verdict yet. The plane's
  API has no read for these runs (`/public/v1/evals/runs/{id}` serves only runs the plane ran
  itself), so point the user to the console to see them.
- `EvalResults.publish(run_name)` is an older call that posts scores without a verdict. Use the
  gated path above for evidence the plane counts.

---

# Platform connection, prompts, tracing, push, runner, CLI

Read this when the task connects the SDK to a FastAIAgent control plane, loads versioned prompts, inspects or exports traces, registers agents, runs a runner, or uses the `fastaiagent` CLI.

Everything works offline without `connect()`: traces go to local SQLite, prompts to the local registry. `connect()` adds platform backends beside the local ones.

## The address rule

NEVER invent, guess or hard-code a platform address. Take it from the user, from `FASTAIAGENT_TARGET`, or from `~/.fastaiagent/credentials.toml`. Do not use `app.fastaiagent.net` — that host is dead and was the default before 1.100.0. Each account has its own address, shown in the console when an API key is created. If you do not have it, ask the user; do not fill a placeholder that looks real.

## connect / disconnect

```signature
fastaiagent.connect(api_key, target=, project=, governance_fail_mode=, auto_register=, console_url=, export_traces=, export_evals=, export_checkpoints=, export_experiments=)
fastaiagent.disconnect()
fastaiagent.push(agent, force=)
fastaiagent.refresh_policy()
```

```python
# needs: a FastAIAgent API key and program address from the user
import os

import fastaiagent as fa

fa.connect(
    api_key=os.environ["FASTAIAGENT_API_KEY"],
    target=os.environ["FASTAIAGENT_TARGET"],
    project="my-project",  # optional
)
# ... run agents; traces are exported in the background ...
fa.disconnect()  # flushes pending spans first
```

- Where the calls go: `connect()` once at startup of the entry point that runs the agents, `disconnect()` in a `finally` at exit (a no-op when never connected). A helper that nothing calls sends no traces; a short script that exits without `disconnect()` can lose the last ones. After a connected run, read the trace back (`GET {target}/public/v1/traces/{trace_id}` with the `X-API-Key` header) before saying it reached the platform. `SKILL.md` has a complete `main.py`.
- `target` is REQUIRED since 1.100.0: the argument, else `FASTAIAGENT_TARGET`, else `ValueError` ("No target. Pass target= or set FASTAIAGENT_TARGET ..."). Don't call `fa.connect(api_key=...)` alone — it raises instead of reaching a default host. A failed resolve leaves the previous connection untouched.
- `target` needs an explicit `http://` or `https://` scheme; `"localhost:7842"` raises `ValueError` (message mentions the scheme). A trailing `/` is stripped.
- `api_key` has no default and Python `connect()` does NOT read `FASTAIAGENT_API_KEY`. Read the env var yourself and pass it, as above. Only the CLI reads that variable.
- Invalid key (HTTP 401) or forbidden (403) raises `PlatformAuthError`. An unreachable plane does NOT raise: the connection is stored, a warning is logged, and traces buffer locally until the plane answers. So `connect()` returning proves nothing about reachability.
- An answer that is not 200/401/403 (e.g. wrong host) logs a warning; the key is unverified.
- `auto_register=True` (default): agents that exist at connect time register with the plane, later agents register on their first run (`run`, `arun`, `stream`, `astream`). Best-effort, never fails a run. Use `auto_register=False` to opt out and register with `agent.push()`.
- `export_traces=False`: connect for policy, prompts, scorers and governance without registering a span exporter (for a runtime that owns its own OTel exporter).
- `governance_fail_mode="closed"` (or `FASTAIAGENT_GOVERNANCE_FAIL_MODE=closed`): a governed agent refuses tool calls when the policy cannot be confirmed. Default `"open"`. Any other value logs a warning and stays open.
- `fa.is_connected` is a lazy module attribute (bool), not a function.
- `fa.refresh_policy()` re-pulls the plane policy (returns its version, or `None` when not connected).

## What a connected agent gets from the plane, and what it sends

The plane authors, stores and monitors; the SDK runs everything in your process. Nothing below
lets the plane stop a run from outside it.

| From the plane | How | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Guardrail rules | Pulled with the policy at `connect()`; applied on every run with no code | Not re-pulled by itself: a rule authored after `connect()` applies after `fa.refresh_policy()`. Details in `guardrails.md`. |
| Approval policies (governance) | Same policy pull | Gate governed tool calls; see `governance_fail_mode` above. |
| Prompts | `PromptRegistry().get(slug)` | See Prompts below. |
| Eval datasets | `Dataset.from_platform(name)` | `Dataset.publish(name)` sends one up. |
| LLM-judge scorers | `Scorer.from_platform(name)` | Returns an `LLMJudge`. Unknown name: `PlatformNotFoundError`. |
| Knowledge-base search | `PlatformKB(kb_id, name=, description=)` | Retrieval runs on the plane; the key needs `kb:read`. |
| Curated memory facts | `PlaneFactBlock` in `fastaiagent.agent.memory_blocks` | Read-only, approved facts. |

| To the plane | When | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Traces, including guardrail spans | In the background while connected | `disconnect()` flushes; `export_traces=False` turns it off. |
| Agent definitions | Auto-registered on the first run, or `agent.push()` | Local guardrails only; plane rules are never echoed back. |
| Eval verdicts | Only gated runs (see `evals.md`) | Metadata only, never inputs or outputs. The key needs `eval:execute`. |
| Datasets, prompts | `Dataset.publish(name)`, `PromptRegistry().publish(...)` | Explicit calls only. |

SDK only, never from the plane: `code` guardrails (`fn=`), `action="reask"`, `guardrail_context`,
`timeout_seconds`. Authoring guardrails, scorers and datasets happens in the console or the plane's
API, not in the SDK.

```signature
fastaiagent.plane_guardrails_for_agent(agent_id)
fastaiagent.Dataset.from_platform(name)
fastaiagent.Dataset.publish(name)
fastaiagent.Scorer.from_platform(name)
fastaiagent.PlatformKB(kb_id, name=, description=)
```

## Connected-agent checklist

Run through this before you say a connected app works. Each step names what proves it.

1. **Key and address from the environment.** `FASTAIAGENT_API_KEY` and `FASTAIAGENT_TARGET`; never
   in code, never printed.
2. **`connect()` in the entry point, `disconnect()` in a `finally`** (`SKILL.md` has the
   `main.py`). `connect()` returning does not prove the plane answered: an unreachable plane only
   logs a warning. A 401 or 403 raises `PlatformAuthError`.
3. **Plane guardrails reached this agent.** Print
   `[g.name for g in fa.plane_guardrails_for_agent(agent.agent_id or agent.name)]`. An empty list
   means one of: none authored; authored after `connect()` (call `fa.refresh_policy()`); scoped to
   another agent; a `code` rule (skipped); or the policy pull failed, which `connect()` and
   `refresh_policy()` log as a warning. Do not report "guardrails are enforced" from an empty list.
4. **Rules scoped to one agent.** Rules attached to agents, and approval policies on tools, are
   matched by the plane's agent id. A connected agent registers on its first run, and that run
   waits up to 5 s for its id when the policy needs it. A warning means it waited longer and
   that run went without them. `agent.push()` after `connect()` registers it up front.
5. **A rule actually fires.** Send one input it should catch and expect `GuardrailBlockedError`
   (or the masked or warned output for `mask` and `warn`). Take that input from the rule (its
   `config`, printed with its name) or ask the user for one; do not generate candidates by
   searching the pattern. A test that proves it names that input. Then read the trace back.
6. **Traces arrived.** `GET {target}/public/v1/traces/{trace_id}` with the `X-API-Key` header
   returns 200, after `disconnect()` has flushed. A finished run gives `result.trace_id`; a
   blocked one raises, and its id is `err.trace_id` on the `GuardrailBlockedError`.
7. **Eval verdicts arrived.** Only gated runs against a real model are sent (`evals.md`, "With a
   platform"); a run a scripted model answered stays local, by design. After
   `disconnect()`, `fastaiagent eval export --status` showing 0 runs waiting means the plane
   confirmed them; `--dry-run` shows what would leave and whether a run is exportable.
8. **Say what you checked.** Name each step you ran and what it printed, and each one you could
   not run (no plane, no rule authored, key without `eval:execute`).

## Credentials resolution

Python: arguments, then `FASTAIAGENT_TARGET` (target only). Nothing else is read.

CLI (`fastaiagent push`, `fastaiagent auth status|env`): the helper `_load_saved_credentials` merges, with environment winning over the file:

| Source | Fields |
|---|---|
| Env: `FASTAIAGENT_API_KEY`, `FASTAIAGENT_TARGET`, `FASTAIAGENT_PROJECT` | api key, target, project |
| File `~/.fastaiagent/credentials.toml` (mode 0600, written by `fastaiagent connect`) | `api_key`, `target`, `project` |
| `--api-key` / `--target` on `fastaiagent push` | override both |

- `fastaiagent connect --api-key ... [--target ...] [--project ...]` calls `connect()`, then saves the file. `--api-key` prompts (hidden) when omitted; it does not read `FASTAIAGENT_API_KEY`. Exit code 1 when the plane is unreachable ("Saved, not verified") or answers a non-plane HTTP code (then nothing is saved).
- `fastaiagent disconnect` deletes the file. `fastaiagent auth status` shows source and masked key; `eval "$(fastaiagent auth env)"` exports the saved values as env vars.
- Other optional env vars: `FASTAIAGENT_CONSOLE_URL` (console origin for deep links, when it differs from the target), `FASTAIAGENT_GOVERNANCE_FAIL_MODE`.

## Prompts

```signature
fastaiagent.PromptRegistry(store=, path=)
fastaiagent.PromptRegistry.register(name, template, fragments=, metadata=, version=, project_id=, created_by=)
fastaiagent.PromptRegistry.register_fragment(name, content)
fastaiagent.PromptRegistry.get(slug, version=, source=)
fastaiagent.PromptRegistry.load(name, version=, alias=, resolve_fragments=)
fastaiagent.PromptRegistry.set_alias(name, version, alias)
fastaiagent.PromptRegistry.publish(slug, content, variables=)
fastaiagent.Prompt.format(**kwargs)
fastaiagent.Prompt.trace_attributes()
```

```python
from fastaiagent import PromptRegistry

reg = PromptRegistry(path="/tmp/fa_platform_ref_prompts.db")
reg.register_fragment(name="tone", content="Be professional.")
reg.register(name="greeting", template="Hello {{name}}. {{@tone}}")
reg.set_alias("greeting", 1, "production")

prompt = reg.get("greeting")  # local registry when not connected
print(prompt.format(name="World"))
print(reg.load("greeting", alias="production").version)
```

- Placeholders are `{{var}}`; fragments are `{{@fragment}}`. `Prompt.format(**kwargs)` is plain string replacement: a missing variable is left in the output as `{{var}}` with NO error — check `prompt.variables` yourself.
- `get(slug, version=None, source="auto")`: `"auto"` uses the platform when connected, else local; `"platform"` raises `PromptNotFoundError` if absent; `"local"` never touches the network. A platform fetch that fails for another reason silently falls back to the local registry under `"auto"`. Platform results are cached 5 minutes per `(slug, version)`; `reg.refresh(slug)` drops the cache.
- `load()` is local only and takes `alias=` (e.g. `"production"`). `get()` has no alias argument.
- Versions are immutable. `register()` without `version=` adds the next version; re-registering an existing `version=` with a different template raises `ValueError`.
- `publish(slug, content)` pushes to the platform and raises `PlatformNotConnectedError` when not connected.
- Pass the `Prompt` object itself as `Agent(system_prompt=prompt)` (not `prompt.format()`, which drops the lineage) and the run stamps `fastaiagent.prompt.*` attributes on its LLM span. Around a foreign framework call, use `fa.trace_context("name", **prompt.trace_attributes())`.
- The registry lives in the local DB (see Tracing); `PromptRegistry(path=...)` points it elsewhere.

## Tracing

Tracing is automatic: every `Agent`/`Chain` run writes spans to local SQLite (`.fastaiagent/local.db`, override with `FASTAIAGENT_LOCAL_DB`). `result.trace_id` identifies the run. Local capture is always full fidelity; filtering happens only on the way out.

```signature
fastaiagent.trace_context(name, **attributes)
fastaiagent.TraceStore(db_path=)
fastaiagent.TraceStore.list_traces(last_hours=, limit=, name_filter=, agent_name=, exclude_sources=)
fastaiagent.TraceStore.get_trace(trace_id)
fastaiagent.trace.add_exporter(exporter)
fastaiagent.enable_otel_capture(framework=)
fastaiagent.disable_otel_capture()
```

```python
import os
import tempfile

os.environ["FASTAIAGENT_LOCAL_DB"] = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "local.db")

from fastaiagent import Agent, TraceStore, trace_context
from fastaiagent.testing import TestModel

agent = Agent(name="demo", system_prompt="Be brief.", llm=TestModel(response="hi"))

with trace_context("my-operation", **{"custom.key": "value"}) as span:
    span.set_attribute("step", "start")
    result = agent.run("hello")

store = TraceStore()
print(result.trace_id, len(store.list_traces(last_hours=1)))
```

- `trace_context` is a context manager yielding an OTel span; nested use nests spans. It needs no connection.
- `list_traces(last_hours=24, limit=100)` defaults hide older traces: pass `last_hours=None` for all time. An unknown keyword only warns (`UserWarning`) and is ignored.
- Tracing is on by default; there is nothing to turn on. Do not set `FASTAIAGENT_TRACE_ENABLED=1` in code or docs.
- `FASTAIAGENT_TRACE_ENABLED=0` is the master switch: no local capture and no export at all (Replay and the UI then have nothing).
- `FASTAIAGENT_TRACE_PAYLOADS=0` keeps prompts, outputs and tool arguments local: they are stripped before spans reach the plane or any `add_exporter` target. It does not reduce what `local.db` holds. An unparseable value counts as off (fails closed).
- `add_exporter(exporter)` adds any OTel `SpanExporter` (Jaeger, Datadog, ...); it is wrapped so payloads are filtered per the settings above.
- `enable_otel_capture()` is the one opt-in call to capture and render spans from third-party OTel/OpenInference instrumentors (including other agent frameworks) in the local store and UI. Call it once at startup; idempotent. It does nothing if `FASTAIAGENT_TRACE_ENABLED` is off. `disable_otel_capture()` only stops normalisation; an attached processor stays attached.
- Other egress switches (all default on, all fail closed when unparseable): `FASTAIAGENT_EXPORT_EVALS`, `FASTAIAGENT_EXPORT_CHECKPOINTS`. `FASTAIAGENT_EXPORT_EXPERIMENTS` defaults off (replay reruns and Playground calls stay local). `connect()` logs the resolved posture once at INFO.
- Unsent spans buffer in `local.db` while the plane is unreachable and drain later. `fastaiagent traces prune` deletes only spans the plane already has.

## Registering agents (`push`)

```signature
fastaiagent.Agent.push(force=)
```

```python
# needs: a connected plane (fa.connect with a key and FASTAIAGENT_TARGET)
import fastaiagent as fa
from fastaiagent.testing import TestModel

agent = fa.Agent(name="support", system_prompt="Help.", llm=TestModel(response="ok"))
result = agent.push()          # same as fa.push(agent)
print(result.agent_id, result.version, result.url)
```

- Requires an active `connect()` and the `agent:write` scope on the key; raises on platform errors (`PlatformNotConnectedError` when not connected). `force=True` is the default and always re-pushes.
- The plane keys agents by name within a project: two live agents with the same name overwrite each other. Give them distinct names.
- A Supervisor worker or Swarm member registers as the agent it was made from (since 1.99.0), without `handoff_to_*` tools.
- Auto-registration (see connect) already does this on first run; use `push()` for deterministic CI/deploy registration.
- CLI: `fastaiagent push --module my_app.agents [--dry-run]` imports the module and pushes every module-level `Agent`, `Supervisor` (lead and workers) and `Swarm` (members). `--dry-run` prints one JSON array of request bodies on stdout, notes on stderr, and contacts nothing. Exit 1 if no agents are found or any push fails.

## Runner

```bash
fastaiagent runner --connect "$FASTAIAGENT_TARGET" --key "$FASTAIAGENT_API_KEY" \
  [--labels k=v ...] [--max-concurrency 4] [--tools module:callable ...]
```

- A long-lived daemon that registers with the plane, heartbeats, pulls live jobs (`live_playground`, `eval_run`) and runs them in your process with your local tools and keys. Ctrl-C / SIGTERM drains in-flight jobs.
- `--connect` and `--key` are both required. It calls `connect()` with the same key so job traces are exported; a bad key exits 1.
- A non-loopback `--connect` must be `https://`; plain `http` exits 2 unless `FASTAIAGENT_RUNNER_ALLOW_INSECURE=1`. Loopback http is allowed.
- `--tools module:callable` imports and calls the callable, which must register your local tools in `ToolRegistry`; only then does the runner advertise `tool_exec`. Without it, plane-dispatched tool calls are not accepted.
- Each job runs in its own request-scoped `job_scope`, so concurrent jobs do not share a connection.

## CLI commands

Run `fastaiagent <command> --help` for flags. Entry point: `fastaiagent` (also `python -m fastaiagent.cli.main`).

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `connect` / `disconnect` | Save / remove platform credentials; verify the key. |
| `auth status` / `auth env` | Show saved credentials and their source / print `export` lines. |
| `push --module M [--dry-run]` | Register agents defined in a module with the plane. |
| `runner --connect --key` | Run a registered runner daemon that pulls live jobs. |
| `version` | SDK version and which optional extras are installed. |
| `migrate` | Copy legacy `traces.db`, `checkpoints.db`, `.prompts/` into `local.db`. |
| `resume` | Resume a suspended execution. |
| `list-pending` | List pending interrupts. |
| `inspect` | Show checkpoint history for an execution. |
| `setup-checkpointer` | Provision the durability backend (SQLite or Postgres). |
| `export-trace --trace-id ID [-o FILE]` | Export one trace as a self-contained JSON file from local SQLite (default `trace.json`). |
| `traces list` / `export` | List recent traces / export a trace. |
| `traces prune` | Delete spans the plane already has, to reclaim space. |
| `traces scrub-secrets` | Remove credentials from spans stored by an older SDK. |
| `traces purge` | Delete trace data from `local.db`. |
| `replay show` / `inspect` / `fork` | Show replay steps / inspect one step / fork a trace at a step, modify, rerun. |
| `eval run` | Run an evaluation and gate on it (non-zero exit for CI; 3 = invalid run). |
| `eval compare` | Compare two persisted eval runs, baseline first. |
| `eval export` | Preview what Agent-CI evidence would leave the machine (`--dry-run`). |
| `eval curate` | Build an eval dataset from captured agent traces. |
| `prompts list` / `diff` | List prompts / diff two versions. |
| `kb list` / `status` / `add` / `clear` / `delete` | Manage local knowledge bases. |
| `mcp serve` | Expose an Agent or Chain as an MCP server over stdio (needs the `mcp` extra). |
| `agent serve` | Serve an Agent or Chain as a FastAPI service (`/run`, `/run/stream`, `/resume`, `/cancel`). Set `FASTAIAGENT_SERVE_TOKEN` for any network-exposed deployment; default bind is `0.0.0.0`. |
| `ui start` / `ui reset-password` | Start the local web UI (default `127.0.0.1:7842`) / reset its login. |
| `learn` / `learn list` / `learn supersede` | Extract durable facts from past traces / list active facts / supersede one. |
| `optimize --agent --dataset` | Eval-driven prompt optimisation loop for an agent. |

Don't call `fastaiagent connect` from CI without `--target` or `FASTAIAGENT_TARGET` — it fails with the no-target error, exit 1.

## Agent Studio from code or the command line (1.102.0)

Not for writing agent code by hand. A platform at 0.20.0 or later can build an agent from a spec you
design: `fastaiagent studio …` (`context`, `new`, `spec validate|push|get`, `show`, `try`, `eval`,
`export`, …) and `fastaiagent.studio.StudioClient` (also `fa.studio`). The `fastaiagent-studio` skill
teaches the loop, the spec and the errors; read that skill, not this paragraph, before you use it.
`StudioError(code, message, status, details)` is a `PlatformError`; a platform without Studio raises
`StudioError("studio_not_available")`.

---

# The `fastaiagent-studio` skill

> Use only when the person wants a NEW agent built, or an agent Studio made changed, inside FastAIAgent Agent Studio from the command line — "build me an order-status agent with Studio", "make a support team in Studio", "change the agent Studio made". You design the agent and write it as a spec; the `fastaiagent studio` commands check it, render the code, try it in Studio's sandbox, keep versions and export a project. Needs a FastAIAgent platform (0.20.0 or later) and an API key with Agent Studio permissions. Not for an agent whose code is in this project, and not for evaluating against a platform dataset, using platform guardrails or connecting an app to the platform: those are the fastaiagent-sdk skill.

# Agent Studio, from the command line

Agent Studio is the FastAIAgent platform's builder: it checks a design, renders real SDK code
from it, tries the agent against sample data, scores eval cases and exports a project. From the
command line **you are the planner**. Studio's own model is never called: you design the agent
with your model and send the design as a **spec**. Studio checks it and does the rest.

After the export the code is the person's. Studio assists; it is not where agents live.

**Is this the right skill?** If the project already has `fastaiagent` code and the person did not
say "Studio", it is not: evaluating that agent (including against a dataset on the platform),
enforcing the platform's guardrails or connecting it to the platform is done in the code. Stop and
use the fastaiagent-sdk skill. Do not ask for Agent Studio permissions for that work.

## Before you start

- A platform **0.20.0 or later** and an API key with `studio:read` and `studio:write` (the
  console's "Agent Studio" key preset has both). Credentials come from `fastaiagent connect`,
  or `FASTAIAGENT_API_KEY` and `FASTAIAGENT_TARGET`. Never ask for a key in chat, never print
  one, never write one into a file.
- Every command takes `--json` and prints one JSON document on stdout; notes and errors go to
  stderr. **Always pass `--json`** and read the document. Exit 0 means it happened; exit 1 means
  it did not (a refusal, a spec with problems, an eval that failed).
- `<draft>` is a draft's id or its name.

## The loop

Do the steps in order. Do not skip step 3.

1. **`fastaiagent studio context --json`** — the project's LLM endpoints, knowledge bases, the
   guardrail names and tool types a spec may use, and the limits. **No LLM endpoint: stop** and
   tell the person to add one in the console; nothing can be made without it. Writes off
   (`environment.studio_writes_allowed` is false): stop and say so.
2. **Read what the person wants.** Read any requirements document yourself. Read any scan or image
   yourself, and say plainly what you could not read.
3. **Lay the design out for the person and wait for a yes.** Say: the shape (one agent, a
   supervisor team, or a swarm), each worker and what it does, each tool and where its data comes
   from, the guardrails, and the eval cases. There is no plan step in the API, so this is where
   the person approves. Never push a spec they have not agreed to.
4. **`studio new --name … --brief "…" --data orders.csv --data-text scan=scan.txt --endpoint <id>`**
   — makes the draft and adds the sample data. Pass `--endpoint` when the project has more than
   one. A PDF or Word file with a text layer can be uploaded as it is; **a scan, a photo or any
   image is refused** (`no_text_layer`): read it yourself, write the text to a file, and pass it
   with `--data-text name=file`. Add `--harness` only when the person wants the prompts and eval
   cases wired to the platform.
5. **Write the spec** (`references/spec.md`), then **`studio spec validate <draft> spec.json
   --json`**. Fix every problem it lists, each names its place. **Read every warning out to the
   person**: a warning does not stop a version, and the person may not want what it says.
6. **`studio spec push <draft> spec.json --note "…" --wait --json`** — makes the next version.
7. **Look, then try, then evaluate:** `studio show <draft> --json` (the blueprint), `studio show
   <draft> --files`, `studio try <draft> "a real question" --json`, `studio eval <draft> --json`.
   Report what happened as it happened: failed cases and their reasons, and cases that "need
   review" because the word rules cannot score them.
8. **To change anything:** `studio spec get <draft> --out spec.json`, edit it, `validate`, `push`.
   A new version is made and the old one is kept. A spec is always sent whole, never a patch.
   Results count for one version: a pass on v1 is not carried to v2, so evaluate again.
9. **`studio export <draft> --out <repo folder>`** — unpacks the project. Run its tests (they run
   offline). Tell the person how to run the agent with their own model key. After the export,
   the code is theirs.

## The rules

- **Never push a spec the person has not agreed to.** The platform cannot know they agreed.
- **Never print or store a key.**
- **A refusal is an answer, not an obstacle.** When a command fails, read `error.code`,
  `error.message` and `error.hint`, tell the person, and stop. Do not retry a refusal, and do not
  look for another way round it (`environment_rule`, `insufficient_scope`, `no_llm_endpoint`,
  `key_has_no_owner`). `references/errors.md` says what each code means.
- **Stale: stop and ask.** If `studio status` says `steps.stale` is true, someone changed the
  draft in the console after the current version was made. Ask the person before changing anything.
- **A team is tried one worker at a time** (`studio try … --worker orders`). Its end-to-end eval
  cases run only from the exported code.
- **Guardrails are not applied in a sandbox trial.** They apply in the exported code. Never tell
  the person a guardrail "passed" because a trial succeeded.
- **Tools answer from sample data in a trial,** never from a live system (except a knowledge-base
  tool, which searches its knowledge base). A passing trial does not prove a REST tool works.
- **Do not invent commands.** There is no `studio plan`, `build`, `refine` or `reset`: planning
  and building from a description, and starting over, are console-only. To start over, push a new
  spec; it makes a new version.
- **Do not ask a draft's model to design for you.** You design; Studio checks and renders.
- Use `--json`, branch on `error.code`, and do not parse the human text.

## Where to read

| You are doing | Read |
|---|---|
| Writing the spec: every field, the tool types, guardrails, eval criteria, worked examples for a single agent, a supervisor team and a swarm | `references/spec.md` |
| Running a command: its options, and the JSON it prints | `references/commands.md` |
| A command failed | `references/errors.md` |

To write the SDK code the exported project is built from, or to change it by hand afterwards, use
the `fastaiagent-sdk` skill.

---

# Writing a spec

A **spec** is the design of one agent, as one JSON object. Studio checks it, renders the SDK
code from it (the spec is the only input to the renderer), and keeps every version. You send it
whole each time (`studio spec push`); there is no partial update. Print the exact JSON Schema
with `fastaiagent studio spec schema`; this page is what a schema cannot say.

Validate before you push: `fastaiagent studio spec validate <draft> spec.json --json`. A
**problem** stops a version; a **warning** does not. Both name their place in `where`.

## The top level

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `spec_version` | `1` |
| `name` | The agent's name in code: `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{2,63}$`. Not the draft's display name. |
| `description` | 1 to 1,000 characters. |
| `architecture` | `single`, `supervisor` or `swarm`. (`chain` is in the schema but is refused.) |
| `system_prompt` | A single agent's prompt, or a supervisor's routing prompt. At least 40 characters. A swarm has none: its workers own theirs. |
| `llm` | `{"endpoint_id": "<id>"}`, an LLM endpoint of the project (`studio context`). The generated code is written for that endpoint's provider and model. |
| `tools` | A single agent's tools. For a team it must be empty: every tool belongs to a worker. |
| `guardrails` | Safety checks on the whole agent (see below). |
| `eval_cases` | **At least 3.** For a team these are the end-to-end cases. |
| `config` | Optional: `max_iterations` (1 to 25, default 10), `temperature` (0 to 2), `max_tokens` (1 to 32000). |
| `workers` | Teams only: **2 to 6**, names unique. |
| `max_delegation_rounds` | Supervisor only, 1 to 8 (default 3). |
| `entrypoint`, `handoffs`, `max_handoffs` | Swarm only. `max_handoffs` is 1 to 16 (default 8). |

A team size a person fixed in the console binds a spec sent here: a different worker count is a
problem that names the fixed size.

## Tools

Every tool has `name` (a lowercase Python identifier, **unique across the whole spec**),
`description` (1 to 500 characters; the agent's model reads it), `parameters`, and optionally
`fixture_ref` (the sample-data file that answers for it in a trial).

`parameters` is flat. Each entry is an object, never a bare string:

```json
{ "order_id": { "type": "string", "description": "the order number" } }
```

`type` is `string`, `integer`, `number` or `boolean`. Parameter names are lowercase identifiers.

| `type` | Extra fields | In the exported code | In a trial |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mock` | `fixture_ref` (required), `match_keys` (each must be one of `parameters`), `default_response` | A lookup over the bundled sample data | The same lookup, served by Studio |
| `rest` | `url` (http or https), `method` (`GET` default, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`), `auth` (`none`, `bearer_env`, `api_key_env`) | A `RESTTool`; the secret is read from the environment | Answered from `fixture_ref` if set |
| `mcp` | `server_url`, `tool_name` | An `MCPTool` | Answered from `fixture_ref` if set |
| `kb` | `kb_id` (a knowledge base from `studio context`) | A `PlatformKB` search; needs a draft made with `--harness` | With `kb_id`: a search of that knowledge base. With `fixture_ref`: sample data |
| `function` | `returns` (`str`, `int`, `float`, `bool`) | A typed stub the developer finishes | Answered from `fixture_ref` if set |

**No tool ever carries a secret.** With `auth: bearer_env` the exported code reads
`TOOL_API_TOKEN`; with `api_key_env` it reads `TOOL_API_KEY`. Never put a key in a spec.

**Sample data must be reachable.** If you uploaded data, at least one tool must read it, and a
`mock` tool names it with `fixture_ref` and the sample file's name (`orders.csv` is `orders`). A
`mock` tool matches rows on `match_keys` (for `order_id`, the row whose `order_id` equals what the
agent passed) and answers `default_response` when no row matches.

## Guardrails

`{"factory": "<name>", "kwargs": {...}}`. An unknown name, a missing required argument or an
extra one is a problem. `studio context` lists the names; these are the arguments:

| Factory | Arguments | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `no_pii` | none | |
| `no_secrets` | none | |
| `no_prompt_injection` | none | |
| `responsible_ai` | none | |
| `openai_moderation` | none | Calls OpenAI's moderation API. The exported agent needs the `openai` package and an OpenAI key, and **blocks every answer without them** |
| `toxicity_check` | optional `threshold` | |
| `cost_limit` | required `max_usd` | |
| `allowed_domains` | required `domains` | |
| `banned_topics` | required `topics` | |
| `allowed_topics` | required `topics` | In a **swarm** it is generated to check the question, not the answer (warning `guardrail_checks_question`) |
| `json_valid` | none | **Warns.** Blocks every answer that is not a JSON document; only for an agent told to answer in JSON |
| `grounded` | required `reference`, optional `threshold` | **Warns.** Checks the answer against a fixed reference text, so answers built from tool results fail |
| `no_hallucination` | required `reference`, optional `threshold` | **Warns.** Same as `grounded` |

Guardrails are **not applied in a sandbox trial**: only in the exported code. A worker with its
own non-empty `guardrails` replaces the team's for that worker; an empty list inherits them.

## Eval cases

```json
{
  "name": "found_1003",
  "input": "What is the status of order 1003?",
  "expected_output": "Order 1003 has shipped.",
  "criteria": { "must_mention": ["1003", "shipped"], "must_not_mention": ["refund"] }
}
```

`name` and `input` are required. `criteria` may hold `must_mention` (a list), `must_not_mention`
(a list) and `behaviour` (a sentence).

**Scoring is by word rules, not a judge.** Every `must_mention` value must appear; no
`must_not_mention` value may; and a case that does not use those rules passes on a 60% word overlap
with `expected_output`. A case with only a `behaviour` can be neither passed nor failed: it reads
**needs review**, and a person reads the answer. A value too short to score (one character, say)
is a warning (`eval_value_unusable`) and is ignored. Prefer specific words ("shipped", "1003") over
common ones. Write at least one case that should be refused or answered "not found".

## Workers

```json
{
  "name": "orders",
  "description": "Order status and delivery questions",
  "system_prompt": "You answer order status questions. Use orders_lookup with the order id and answer briefly.",
  "tools": [],
  "guardrails": [],
  "eval_cases": []
}
```

`name` is a lowercase identifier, unique in the spec; `description` (1 to 500) is what a supervisor
or a peer reads to choose; `system_prompt` is at least 40 characters. Optional: `llm_endpoint_id`
(another endpoint of the project), `max_iterations`. A worker's own `eval_cases` are scored in a
sandbox, one worker at a time; give each worker at least one, or `studio eval --worker` refuses
that worker (`worker_has_no_cases`).

## Swarms

Peers hand control to each other. Name an `entrypoint` (the first worker; it defaults to the first
listed) and list each allowed handoff as `{"from_worker", "to_worker", "when"}`. A worker cannot
hand off to itself, and **every worker must be reachable from the entrypoint**; an unreachable one is
a problem. A swarm has no `system_prompt`.

## Warnings

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `guardrail_blocks_output` | A guardrail that will block every answer this agent gives (`json_valid`, `grounded`, `no_hallucination`) |
| `guardrail_checks_question` | In a swarm, `allowed_topics` is generated to check the question |
| `eval_value_unusable` | An eval value too short to score reliably; it is ignored |
| `eval_dataset_not_updated` | The draft has a linked eval dataset and the spec carries different cases; this version uses the spec's cases |

Nothing is changed behind your back: the spec that is checked is the spec that is rendered.

## Example: one agent

Sample data: `orders.csv` with `order_id`, `status`, `total`.

```json spec
{
  "spec_version": 1,
  "name": "order-status-bot",
  "description": "Answers questions about customer orders from the uploaded orders data.",
  "architecture": "single",
  "system_prompt": "You answer order-status questions for customers. Use the orders_lookup tool with the order id. If the order is not found, say so plainly. Never reveal one customer's order to another. Answer in one or two sentences.",
  "llm": { "endpoint_id": "ENDPOINT_ID" },
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "mock",
      "name": "orders_lookup",
      "description": "Look up one order by its id",
      "parameters": { "order_id": { "type": "string", "description": "the order number" } },
      "fixture_ref": "orders",
      "match_keys": ["order_id"],
      "default_response": "No order with that id."
    }
  ],
  "guardrails": [{ "factory": "no_pii", "kwargs": {} }],
  "eval_cases": [
    { "name": "found_1003", "input": "What is the status of order 1003?", "criteria": { "must_mention": ["1003", "shipped"] } },
    { "name": "missing_9999", "input": "Where is order 9999?", "criteria": { "behaviour": "says plainly that no such order was found" } },
    { "name": "delivered_1004", "input": "Has order 1004 arrived?", "criteria": { "must_mention": ["1004", "delivered"] } }
  ]
}
```

## Example: a supervisor team

A supervisor routes each request to one worker and gives the answer. Every tool is a worker's.

```json spec
{
  "spec_version": 1,
  "name": "support-triage-team",
  "description": "Routes a support request to the orders or the billing specialist.",
  "architecture": "supervisor",
  "system_prompt": "You route each customer request to the right specialist, orders or billing, then give the customer their answer in one or two sentences.",
  "llm": { "endpoint_id": "ENDPOINT_ID" },
  "max_delegation_rounds": 3,
  "tools": [],
  "guardrails": [],
  "workers": [
    {
      "name": "orders",
      "description": "Order status and delivery questions",
      "system_prompt": "You answer order status questions. Use orders_lookup with the order id and answer briefly.",
      "tools": [
        {
          "type": "mock",
          "name": "orders_lookup",
          "description": "Look up one order by its id",
          "parameters": { "order_id": { "type": "string", "description": "the order number" } },
          "fixture_ref": "orders",
          "match_keys": ["order_id"],
          "default_response": "No order with that id."
        }
      ],
      "eval_cases": [
        { "name": "orders_1003", "input": "Where is order 1003?", "criteria": { "must_mention": ["1003", "shipped"] } }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "billing",
      "description": "What an order cost",
      "system_prompt": "You answer questions about what an order cost. Use billing_lookup with the order id and answer briefly.",
      "tools": [
        {
          "type": "mock",
          "name": "billing_lookup",
          "description": "Look up what one order cost",
          "parameters": { "order_id": { "type": "string", "description": "the order number" } },
          "fixture_ref": "orders",
          "match_keys": ["order_id"],
          "default_response": "No order with that id."
        }
      ],
      "eval_cases": [
        { "name": "billing_1002", "input": "What did order 1002 cost?", "criteria": { "must_mention": ["89"] } }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "eval_cases": [
    { "name": "end_to_end_status", "input": "Where is order 1003?" },
    { "name": "end_to_end_cost", "input": "What did order 1002 cost?" },
    { "name": "end_to_end_unknown", "input": "Where is order 9999?" }
  ]
}
```

## Example: a swarm

```json spec
{
  "spec_version": 1,
  "name": "support-swarm",
  "description": "Peers that hand a customer to whoever can help, starting with orders.",
  "architecture": "swarm",
  "llm": { "endpoint_id": "ENDPOINT_ID" },
  "entrypoint": "orders",
  "max_handoffs": 6,
  "tools": [],
  "guardrails": [{ "factory": "no_pii", "kwargs": {} }],
  "workers": [
    {
      "name": "orders",
      "description": "Order status. Hands billing questions to billing.",
      "system_prompt": "You answer order status questions with orders_lookup. If the customer asks what an order cost, hand off to billing.",
      "tools": [
        {
          "type": "mock",
          "name": "orders_lookup",
          "description": "Look up one order by its id",
          "parameters": { "order_id": { "type": "string", "description": "the order number" } },
          "fixture_ref": "orders",
          "match_keys": ["order_id"],
          "default_response": "No order with that id."
        }
      ],
      "eval_cases": [
```
